Subject: Redwood US privacy addendum — confirmation of SP role + subprocessors

Tessa,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. Our legal team reviewed the draft US privacy addendum you sent and had two items they need clarified before we can circulate internally:

1) Role label: The draft uses "service provider" language but also references "processor" in a few places. For our procurement checklist we need an explicit statement that Redwood will act as a "Service Provider" under California (CCPA/CPRA) and the other US state statutes (i.e., no resale/sale exceptions). Can you confirm?

2) Subprocessors/onshore fallback: We need a current inventory of subprocessors and an onshore fallback commitment (or plan) for telemetry and access to logs for incident response. If you can point us to SOC 2 evidence and the subprocessors spreadsheet that would speed sign-off.

Attached is the intake form our contracts team uses. Can you or someone on your privacy team confirm by EOD Friday? We're targeting signature next week.

Appreciate it,

Dan Liu

Dan — thanks, and great meeting earlier. Short answers up front:

• Role: Redwood confirms we will accept the "Service Provider" designation for CCPA/CPRA and equivalent US state privacy addenda; we will not assert a "reseller" or "sale" position for customer content.

• Subprocessors: attaching an up-to-date inventory (see subprocessors_inventory.xlsx). We also have SOC 2 Type II and continuous penetration testing reports; I can share a redacted bundle via your secure link.

I've attached a clean copy of the US addendum with one-line edits to keep the SP language consistent (redwood-us-privacy-addendum-draft.docx). Two asks for your team: 1) Please confirm whether you need Redwood to include an explicit onshore-fallback SLA for log access (we can offer a 48-72 hour technical fallback window with onshore processing on request), and 2) whether your procurement prefers a general subprocessors notification cadence (30 days) or per-change approval for high-risk vendors.

If you want, I can loop in our legal/privacy lead (Karthik) for any redlines.

Best,

Tessa — thanks for flagging. A few operational/legal notes: 

1) "Service Provider" confirmation: safe to confirm, but avoid absolute "no resale" language that could be interpreted to limit telemetry uses. Recommend: "Redwood confirms it will operate as a Service Provider under California and applicable US state privacy laws with respect to Customer Personal Information and will not sell such data." That balances buyer comfort and our telemetry needs.

2) Onshore fallback: 48–72 hours is reasonable for an availability fallback, but we should qualify it as an operational escalation requiring an approved change order for long-term obligations. Proposed clause: "Redwood will provide onshore processing and prioritized access for incident response within 48–72 hours upon Customer request where technically feasible; extended onshore residency commitments will be subject to commercial agreement."

3) Subprocessor evidence: attach the redacted subprocessors_inventory.xlsx (remove account-specific IPs) and provide a link to our SOC 2 summary + a redacted pen test executive summary. For MedHaven, offer a secure share link (we'll produce a signed NDA if required).

4) Notification cadence: default 30-day notice with a high-risk exception that triggers direct notification and 10-business-day pause for review—good compromise.

I'll make the edits in the draft and mark the legal-approved language. Karthik, please confirm there are no regulatory blockers on characterization or the 48–72 hr fallback.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Director, Legal — Redwood Inference

Dan/Emily/Lisa — Karthik here from Redwood legal. Appreciate the detailed intake. To summarize our position and next steps so procurement has a single record: 

• Role: Redwood confirms it will be designated a "Service Provider" with respect to Customer Personal Information under the CCPA/CPRA and other applicable US state privacy statutes. We will not engage in "sale" of Customer Personal Information.

• Subprocessors & evidence: Please find the attached redacted subprocessors inventory (same spreadsheet Tessa shared). We will provide SOC 2 Type II summary and a redacted pen test executive summary via your secure portal — please confirm a link or SFTP destination and we'll push the bundle.

• Onshore fallback: Redwood can commit to providing prioritized onshore processing and support for incident response within a 48–72 hour window upon formal request and activation of our incident escalation procedure. For ongoing onshore-only residency or long-term contractual residency guarantees, we will require a change order and may propose associated commercial terms.

• Notification cadence: Default 30-day notice for subprocessor changes with a high-risk class that triggers direct notification and a 10-business-day review pause.

If MedHaven is fine with the above, we can incorporate the language into the US privacy addendum (attached) and issue a redline for your counsel to review. Production target: redline to you by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
